nights.text: Someone has started leaving things under the door at night. Seven minutes of quiet, please. I want to hear who it is.

note.text: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately.

quest.done: Seven minutes, and a soft scrape at the door. Only a moth with a letter. It would not say who sent it.

keepsake.name: A moth-light letter
keepsake.description: Unsigned. Smells faintly of rain and somebody else's kitchen.

nights.text: The moon is nearly round tonight. I should leave something by the door for whoever writes. A seed, or a reply?

options.label: A seed
options.reply: A seed, then. Nobody has ever been annoyed by a seed. I will put it on the mat.
options.later: The seed is gone from the mat. In its place, a small dry leaf. I take this as manners.

options.label: A reply
options.reply: A reply. Yes. I shall keep it short, in case the moth reads over my shoulder.
options.later: I wrote only 'Hello, who is it?' and slid it out. It has not come back. I keep checking the mat.

nights.text: The clocks went back, I hear. One extra hour tonight. I have put it by the kettle, in case someone needs it.

note.text: An hour is a small room. Leave the door open and see who comes in.

nights.text: The moon is full and very pleased with itself. I counted the things on the mat this morning. Still no name, only a damp leaf.
extras: The lamp has gone amber for the autumn. I did not ask it to. I think it just felt the season.
I mended one cloak button today. The other buttons watched and seem to be thinking about it.
The kettle has a new sound this week, a small cough before the whistle. I have decided it is polite.
Cold nose this morning. Good news: the burrow is still exactly where I left it.

nights.text: The letter-writer left a second note, but the ink ran in the damp. Remember something for me, and I will try to remember what it said.
extras: The first proper frost is somewhere close. I can smell it, like a cold coin.
I swept the leaves off the step. They came back in a better arrangement.
The moth sat on the lampshade all evening, reading. I did not like to ask what.
Soup tonight. I tasted it three times, to be fair to it.

note.text: A small light kept burning is a kind of letter to whoever is still out walking.

quest.done: There. Held fast. The ink has dried, and the note says only: keep the lamp lit. I would have done that anyway.

keepsake.name: A smudged note
keepsake.description: Two words legible, a third lost to damp. It smells of moth wing and cold air.

nights.text: I have kept the lamp lit, as the note said. The moth approves. I still do not know who was asking.
extras: Acorns are dropping on the path tonight, like small, polite knocks.
The wool socks came out of the chest today. They remembered me fondly.
I counted my cloak buttons twice. The answer was the same both times, which is all I ask.
The wind tried the door at dusk, then thought better of it.

nights.text: The mat was bare this morning, not even a leaf. I checked twice, then once more to be fair to the mat.
extras: The moon is past its fullest and has begun to lean. I find it restful to watch something take its time.
A good dark evening for jam on bread. The dark did not ask for jam, but it seemed to approve.
I shook out the blue blanket and a whole summer afternoon fell out of it. Just a small one.
The chimney has started humming when the wind turns north. We are both getting used to it.

note.text: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: its loveliness increases; it will never pass into nothingness.

nights.text: The moth is back on the lampshade, and it ought to have a name. I am poor at names. What shall we call it?
extras: The last of the pears went soft on the sill. I gave them a respectful send-off, with a spoon.
It is dark before supper now. I have started eating by lamplight and calling it a feast.
There is mist on the path tonight. It is only borrowing the road, I think.
The stairs were chilly on my feet this morning. The wool socks were ready, which I took as friendship.

options.label: Wick
options.reply: Wick. Short, warm, and it sits near the lamp anyway. I think it likes it. It did not leave.
options.later: I called it Wick across the room today. A wing twitched. Either it knows, or it was a draught.

options.label: Mister Dusk
options.reply: Mister Dusk. Very grand. I shall use the full name, and bow slightly. The moth bowed back, I think.
options.later: Mister Dusk has taken the good corner of the lampshade. I did not offer it. It simply expected it.
